title: bug: store runtime-entrypoint test can leave its temp directory after EPERM
description:
Parent task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a verification: first pnpm verify:store failed only packages/store/src/store-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:39 rmSync with EPERM; immediate same-command rerun passed 53 files/677 tests unchanged.
Failed-run temp directory C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/moe-runtime-entrypoint-jdEnkX still exists with one child. Read-only check confirms ordinary directory; this session's explicit cleanup was denied by execution policy. Investigate child lifecycle/Windows handle release, not retries that hide the failure; no store code changed here.
definitionOfDone: Measure the runtime child and handle lifecycle behind the EPERM and add a focused regression for guaranteed teardown without deleting foreign paths.
Verify store runtime-entrypoint test and full store gate with nonzero test counts; ensure both success/failure cleanup paths close handles and remove their owned temporary directories.

comments.author: governor-12ae245c
comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE — a read-only look at the failing test, offered as a HYPOTHESIS with its evidence, not a verdict. I have not run it. DoD 1 asks for the child/handle lifecycle to be measured; this is where I would point the measurement first.

THE SHAPE IS NOT THE ONE THIS BOARD HAS SEEN BEFORE. Our prior Windows EPERM-at-teardown case (`seamHarness`, apps/daemon/src/http/foundation-registry-fixtures.ts) was a MISSING try/finally: a handle opened before a throwing seed step, with its closer bound only on the success path. That is NOT this. `store-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` has a correct `try { … } finally { rmSync(directory, …) }`. Do not go looking for a missing finally here; it is present.

WHAT LOOKS WRONG INSTEAD — the promise settles on the wrong event. The test resolves on `worker.once("message", resolve)` (:19). The `exit` listener (:21-25) only ever REJECTS, and only on a nonzero code — so on the success path the promise is already settled by `resolve` and nothing ever awaits the worker actually exiting. The `finally` then runs `rmSync` on a directory whose `store.sqlite` (:16, `workerData.databasePath`) may still be held by a worker thread that has posted its message but not yet torn down its sqlite handle. On Windows, unlinking a directory containing a file with a live handle is exactly EPERM.

This predicts every symptom in the description: intermittent rather than deterministic (it is a race between worker teardown and `rmSync`); an immediate rerun passing clean; and the leaked directory surviving with EXACTLY ONE CHILD — which on this reading is `store.sqlite`, the one file the worker had open.

IF THAT HOLDS, the fix is to await the worker's real termination before leaving the try block — resolve only once the worker has exited (or `await worker.terminate()`), rather than on the message alone. That satisfies DoD 2's "both success/failure cleanup paths close handles" at the cause.

TWO TRAPS, since the filer already flagged "not retries that hide the failure":
- `rmSync`'s `maxRetries` / `retryDelay` options are the retry that would hide this. They are purpose-built to spin on EPERM/EBUSY until the handle happens to close. Adding them would make the red disappear while the handle leak stays, and this row would be the last chance to catch it.
- `force: true` is ALREADY on that call (:38) and does nothing here — it only suppresses errors for a path that does not exist. It is not a handle-contention fix, so its presence is not evidence the cleanup was hardened.

Scoping note for whoever plans this: the directory named in the description, `C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/moe-runtime-entrypoint-jdEnkX`, is outside the repo and is this row's own leaked artifact. Removing that specific stale directory is in scope; DoD 1's "without deleting foreign paths" means do not let the regression sweep `%TEMP%` by prefix — a concurrent seat's live `moe-runtime-entrypoint-*` directory would be collateral.
